sanskrit: kṛtyā hy etā ghorarūpā mohayanty avicakṣaṇān rajasy antarhitā mūrtir indriyāṇāṃ sanātanī
english: For these women are dread enchantments that bewilder the undiscerning; the eternal embodiment of the senses lies hidden within passion (rajas).

sanskrit: tasmāt tarṣātmakād rāgād bījāj jāyanti jantavaḥ svadehajān asvasaṃjñān yadvad aṅgāt kṛmīṃs tyajet svasaṃjñān asvajāṃs tadvat sutasaṃjñān kṛmīṃs tyajet
english: From craving-natured desire, as from a seed, creatures are born. As a man casts off the worms bred from his own body, knowing them as no part of himself, so should he renounce those worms called 'sons'—deeming them his own yet truly not his own.

sanskrit: śukrato rasataś caiva snehāj jāyanti jantavaḥ svabhāvāt karmayogād vā tān upekṣeta buddhimān
english: Creatures are born from seed, from sap, and from affection, whether by nature or by the conjunction of past deeds; the wise man should regard them with detachment.

sanskrit: rajas tamasi paryastaṃ sattvaṃ tamasi saṃsthitam jñānādhiṣṭhānam ajñānaṃ buddhyahaṃkāralakṣaṇam
english: Passion (rajas) is overlaid upon darkness (tamas), and goodness (sattva) too abides in darkness; ignorance, founded upon knowledge, is marked by intellect and the sense of 'I.'

sanskrit: tad bījaṃ dehinām āhus tad bījaṃ jīvasaṃjñitam karmaṇā kālayuktena saṃsāraparivartakam
english: This, they declare, is the seed of embodied beings; this seed is named the living self (jīva), which, through action joined to time, keeps the wheel of saṃsāra turning.

sanskrit: ramaty ayaṃ yathā svapne manasā dehavān iva karmagarbhair guṇair dehī garbhe tad upapadyate
english: As one disports in a dream by the mind alone, as though possessed of a body, so the embodied self, through the qualities that hold the germ of his deeds, comes to be lodged within a womb.

sanskrit: karmaṇā bījabhūtena codyate yad yad indriyam jāyate tad ahaṃkārād rāgayuktena cetasā
english: Whatever sense is impelled by deed grown into a seed, that sense arises out of the sense of 'I,' through a mind charged with desire.

sanskrit: śabdarāgāc chrotram asya jāyate bhāvitātmanaḥ rūparāgāt tathā cakṣur ghrāṇaṃ gandhacikīrṣayā
english: From his craving for sound, the ear of this self that has been shaped by desire is born; from craving for form, the eye; and the nose, from the wish to seize upon scent.

sanskrit: sparśanebhyas tathā vāyuḥ prāṇāpānavyapāśrayaḥ vyānodānau samānaś ca pañcadhā dehayāpanā
english: From the cravings for touch arises the vital air, resting upon prāṇa and apāna; and vyāna, udāna, and samāna—fivefold, sustaining the body in its course.

sanskrit: saṃjātair jāyate gātraiḥ karmajair brahmaṇā vṛtaḥ duḥkhādyantair duḥkhamadhyair naraḥ śārīramānasaiḥ
english: With limbs thus born, sprung from deeds and enveloped by Brahman, the man comes into being—amid sufferings of body and mind, sorrowful at their beginning, their middle, and their end.

sanskrit: duḥkhaṃ vidyād upādānād abhimānāc ca vardhate tyāgāt tebhyo nirodhaḥ syān nirodhajño vimucyate
english: Let him know that suffering arises from grasping, and grows through self-conceit; by renouncing these there comes its cessation, and he who knows that cessation is set free.

sanskrit: indriyāṇāṃ rajasy eva prabhavapralayāv ubhau parīkṣya saṃcared vidvān yathāvac chāstracakṣuṣā
english: Both the rising and the dissolution of the senses lie within passion alone; having examined this, let the wise man move through the world rightly, with the eye of scripture.

sanskrit: jñānendriyāṇīndriyārthān nopasarpanty atarṣulam jñātaiś ca kāraṇair dehī na dehaṃ punar arhati
english: The organs of knowledge do not draw their objects toward the man free of craving; and once their causes are understood, the embodied self need take on a body no more.

sanskrit: gurur uvāca atropāyaṃ pravakṣyāmi yathāvac chāstracakṣuṣā tad vijñānāc caran prājñaḥ prāpnuyāt paramāṃ gatim
english: The teacher said: Herein I shall declare the means, rightly, with the eye of scripture; the wise man who walks by that understanding may attain the supreme goal.

sanskrit: sarveṣām eva bhūtānāṃ puruṣaḥ śreṣṭha ucyate puruṣebhyo dvijān āhur dvijebhyo mantravādinaḥ
english: Of all beings, man is said to be the highest; above men they place the twice-born, and above the twice-born, the reciters of the sacred mantras.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtaviśiṣṭās te sarvajñāḥ sarvadarśinaḥ brāhmaṇā vedatattvajñās tattvārthagatiniścayāḥ
english: Surpassing all beings, all-knowing and all-seeing, are the Brāhmaṇas who know the truth of the Vedas, sure in their grasp of the meaning of reality.

sanskrit: netrahīno yathā hy ekaḥ kṛcchrāṇi labhate 'dhvani jñānahīnas tathā loke tasmāj jñānavido 'dhikāḥ
english: As a man bereft of eyes meets hardship upon the road, so does the man bereft of knowledge in the world; therefore the knowers of wisdom stand above the rest.

sanskrit: tāṃs tān upāsate dharmān dharmakāmā yathāgamam na tv eṣām arthasāmānyam antareṇa guṇān imān
english: Those who long for righteousness honor these several duties according to scripture; yet for them there is no common attainment of their aim apart from these virtues.

sanskrit: vāgdehamanasāṃ śaucaṃ kṣamā satyaṃ dhṛtiḥ smṛtiḥ sarvadharmeṣu dharmajñā jñāpayanti guṇān imān
english: Purity of speech, body, and mind; patience, truth, steadfastness, and mindfulness—amid all duties the knowers of righteousness proclaim these to be the virtues.

sanskrit: yad idaṃ brahmaṇo rūpaṃ brahmacaryam iti smṛtam paraṃ tat sarvabhūtebhyas tena yānti parāṃ gatim
english: That form of Brahman which is remembered as chastity (brahmacarya) is the highest of all things; by it men go to the supreme goal.

sanskrit: liṅgasaṃyogahīnaṃ yac charīrasparśavarjitam śrotreṇa śravaṇaṃ caiva cakṣuṣā caiva darśanam
english: That which is free from the union of the sexes, devoid of bodily contact—as well as the hearing done by the ear and the seeing done by the eye—

sanskrit: jihvayā rasanaṃ yac ca tad eva parivarjitam buddhyā ca vyavasāyena brahmacaryam akalmaṣam
english: and the tasting done by the tongue—when all this too is renounced, then, through the intellect's firm resolve, chastity becomes stainless.

sanskrit: samyagvṛttir brahmalokaṃ prāpnuyān madhyamaḥ surān dvijāgryo jāyate vidvān kanyasīṃ vṛttim āsthitaḥ
english: He of perfect conduct attains the world of Brahman; he of middling conduct, the gods; and the learned one who holds to the least of these courses is born a foremost twice-born.

sanskrit: suduṣkaraṃ brahmacaryam upāyaṃ tatra me śṛṇu saṃpravṛttam udīrṇaṃ ca nigṛhṇīyād dvijo manaḥ
english: Most arduous is chastity; hear from me the means thereto: the twice-born should restrain his mind whether it has merely stirred or has fully risen up.

sanskrit: yoṣitāṃ na kathāḥ śrāvyā na nirīkṣyā nirambarāḥ kadā cid darśanād āsāṃ durbalān āviśed rajaḥ
english: Talk of women should not be listened to, nor should they be gazed upon unclothed; for at the mere sight of them passion may at some moment enter the weak.

sanskrit: rāgotpattau caret kṛcchram ahnas triḥ praviśed apaḥ magnaḥ svapne ca manasā trir japed aghamarṣaṇam
english: Should desire arise, let him perform the penance of hardship, entering the water three times in a day; and if submerged within a dream, let him recite the Aghamarṣaṇa thrice in his mind.

sanskrit: pāpmānaṃ nirdahed evam antarbhūtaṃ rajomayam jñānayuktena manasā saṃtatena vicakṣaṇaḥ
english: Thus let the discerning man burn away the evil dwelling within, made of passion, with a mind joined to knowledge and unbroken in its effort.

sanskrit: kuṇapāmedhyasaṃyuktaṃ yadvad acchidrabandhanam tadvad dehagataṃ vidyād ātmānaṃ dehabandhanam
english: As a vessel without flaw is bound up with what is foul and corpse-like, so let him know the self that has entered the body to be bound fast to that body.

sanskrit: vātapittakaphān raktaṃ tvaṅmāṃsaṃ snāyum asthi ca majjāṃ caiva sirājālais tarpayanti rasā nṛṇām
english: Through their network of channels the bodily fluids of men nourish the wind, bile, and phlegm, the blood, the skin and flesh, the sinew, the bone, and the marrow.

sanskrit: daśa vidyād dhamanyo 'tra pañcendriyaguṇāvahāḥ yābhiḥ sūkṣmāḥ pratāyante dhamanyo 'nyāḥ sahasraśaḥ
english: Let him know that there are ten great vessels here, carrying the properties of the five senses; from these, other subtle vessels spread out by the thousands.

sanskrit: evam etāḥ sirānadyo rasodā dehasāgaram tarpayanti yathākālam āpagā iva sāgaram
english: Thus these vessel-rivers, bearing the bodily fluids, nourish the ocean of the body in due season, as the rivers nourish the sea.

sanskrit: madhye ca hṛdayasyaikā sirā tv atra manovahā śukraṃ saṃkalpajaṃ nṝṇāṃ sarvagātrair vimuñcati
english: And in the midst of the heart is one vessel, the bearer of the mind, which releases through all the limbs the seed of men born of intention (saṃkalpa).

sanskrit: sarvagātrapratāyinyas tasyā hy anugatāḥ sirāḥ netrayoḥ pratipadyante vahantyas taijasaṃ guṇam
english: The vessels that follow from it, spreading through all the limbs, reach the two eyes, carrying the fiery quality.

sanskrit: payasy antarhitaṃ sarpir yadvan nirmathyate khajaiḥ śukraṃ nirmathyate tadvad dehasaṃkalpajaiḥ khajaiḥ
english: As the butter hidden within milk is churned forth by the churning-sticks, so is the seed churned forth by the churning-sticks born of the body's intentions.

sanskrit: svapne 'py evaṃ yathābhyeti manaḥsaṃkalpajaṃ rajaḥ śukram asparśajaṃ dehāt sṛjanty asya manovahā
english: Even in dream, just as the passion born of the mind's intention comes upon him, so do the mind-bearing vessels release from his body the seed that arose without any touch.

sanskrit: maharṣir bhagavān atrir veda tac chukrasaṃbhavam tribījam indradaivatyaṃ tasmād indriyam ucyate
english: The great sage, the blessed Atri, knew that origin of the seed: threefold in its source and presided over by Indra; for that reason it is called indriya (sense).

sanskrit: ye vai śukragatiṃ vidyur bhūtasaṃkarakārikām virāgā dagdhadoṣās te nāpnuyur dehasaṃbhavam
english: Those who know the course of the seed, which works the commingling of beings, being free of passion and having burned away their faults, would take on no further birth in a body.

sanskrit: guṇānāṃ sāmyam āgamya manasaiva manovaham dehakarma nudan prāṇān antakāle vimucyate
english: Having reached the equipoise of the guṇas, by the mind alone driving off the mind-borne breaths and the body's activity, a man is set free at the hour of his end.

sanskrit: bhavitā manaso jñānaṃ mana eva pratāyate jyotiṣmad virajo divyam atra siddhaṃ mahātmanām
english: Knowledge will arise within the mind, and from the mind alone it spreads forth—radiant, free of passion, and divine; this, for the great-souled, is the accomplishment attained here.

sanskrit: tasmāt tad avighātāya karma kuryād akalmaṣam rajas tamaś ca hitveha na tiryaggatim āpnuyāt
english: Therefore, to keep that knowledge unhindered, let him perform stainless action; and casting off passion and darkness in this life, he shall not pass into the state of beasts.

sanskrit: taruṇādhigataṃ jñānaṃ jarādurbalatāṃ gatam paripakvabuddhiḥ kālena ādatte mānasaṃ balam
english: The knowledge gained in youth, though it has passed into the feebleness of age, is in time received anew as strength of mind by one whose understanding has ripened.

sanskrit: sudurgam iva panthānam atītya guṇabandhanam yadā paśyet tadā doṣān atītyāmṛtam aśnute
english: When, having crossed the bondage of the guṇas as one crosses a most difficult road, he beholds the faults for what they are, then, transcending them, he tastes the deathless.

sanskrit: gurur uvāca duranteṣv indriyārtheṣu saktāḥ sīdanti jantavaḥ ye tv asaktā mahātmānas te yānti paramāṃ gatim
english: The teacher said: Clinging to the objects of sense, whose end is grievous, creatures sink down; but the great-souled who do not cling go to the supreme goal.

sanskrit: janmamṛtyujarāduḥkhair vyādhibhir manasaḥ klamaiḥ dṛṣṭvemaṃ saṃtataṃ lokaṃ ghaṭen mokṣāya buddhimān
english: Beholding this world held continuously in the grip of birth, death, old age, sorrow, disease, and the mind's weariness, let the wise man strive for liberation (mokṣa).

sanskrit: vāṅmanobhyāṃ śarīreṇa śuciḥ syād anahaṃkṛtaḥ praśānto jñānavān bhikṣur nirapekṣaś caret sukham
english: Pure in speech, mind, and body, free of the sense of 'I,' tranquil and possessed of knowledge, let the mendicant move through the world happily, expecting nothing.

sanskrit: atha vā manasaḥ saṅgaṃ paśyed bhūtānukampayā atrāpy upekṣāṃ kurvīta jñātvā karmaphalaṃ jagat
english: Or, should he perceive an attachment of the mind arising out of compassion for living beings, in this too let him practice detachment, knowing the world to be the fruit of action.

sanskrit: yat kṛtaṃ prāk śubhaṃ karma pāpaṃ vā tad upāśnute tasmāc chubhāni karmāṇi kuryād vāgbuddhikarmabhiḥ
english: Whatever deed was done before, whether good or evil, that he must reap; therefore let him do good deeds with speech, mind, and act.

sanskrit: ahiṃsā satyavacanaṃ sarvabhūteṣu cārjavam kṣamā caivāpramādaś ca yasyaite sa sukhī bhavet
english: Non-violence, truthful speech, uprightness toward all beings, patience, and vigilance—he in whom these dwell shall be happy.

sanskrit: yaś cainaṃ paramaṃ dharmaṃ sarvabhūtasukhāvaham duḥkhān niḥsaraṇaṃ veda sa tattvajñaḥ sukhī bhavet
english: And he who knows this supreme dharma, the bringer of happiness to all beings and the way out of suffering, that knower of truth shall be happy.

sanskrit: tasmāt samāhitaṃ buddhyā mano bhūteṣu dhārayet nāpadhyāyen na spṛhayen nābaddhaṃ cintayed asat
english: Therefore, his mind composed by the intellect, let him hold it steady toward all beings; let him not brood with malice, nor crave, nor dwell unmoored upon what is false.

sanskrit: avāgyogaprayogeṇa manojñaṃ saṃpravartate vivakṣatā vā sadvākyaṃ dharmaṃ sūkṣmam avekṣatā satyāṃ vācam ahiṃsrāṃ ca vaded anapavādinīm
english: Through the practice of silence the mind grows agreeable; or, when one wishes to speak good words, regarding the subtle nature of dharma, let him utter speech that is true, harmless, and free of slander.

sanskrit: kalkāpetām aparuṣām anṛśaṃsām apaiśunām īdṛg alpaṃ ca vaktavyam avikṣiptena cetasā
english: Free of guile, ungentle never, without cruelty and without backbiting—such speech, and that but little, should be uttered with an undistracted mind.

sanskrit: vākprabuddho hi saṃrāgād virāgād vyāhared yadi buddhyā hy anigṛhītena manasā karma tāmasam rajobhūtair hi karaṇaiḥ karmaṇā pratipadyate
english: For if one roused to speech were to speak out of strong passion or out of aversion, then, with a mind ungoverned by the intellect, he undertakes an action steeped in darkness; through organs grown full of passion he is bound by his deed.

sanskrit: sa duḥkhaṃ prāpya loke 'smin narakāyopapadyate tasmān manovākśarīrair ācared dhairyam ātmanaḥ
english: Having met with sorrow in this world, he goes on to hell; therefore let him practice the self-mastery of his own being through mind, speech, and body.

sanskrit: prakīrṇameṣabhāro hi yadvad dhāryeta dasyubhiḥ pratilomāṃ diśaṃ buddhvā saṃsāram abudhās tathā
english: As a scattered burden of sheep might be driven off by robbers, so are the unknowing carried along through saṃsāra, mistaking the contrary direction for the right.

sanskrit: tān eva ca yathā dasyūn kṣiptvā gacchec chivāṃ diśam tathā rajastamaḥkarmāṇy utsṛjya prāpnuyāt sukham
english: And as one might cast off those very robbers and go toward the auspicious quarter, so, abandoning the works of passion and darkness, a man may attain to bliss.

sanskrit: niḥsaṃdigdham anīho vai muktaḥ sarvaparigrahaiḥ viviktacārī laghvāśī tapasvī niyatendriyaḥ
english: Free of doubt, without longing, released from all possessions, walking in solitude, eating sparingly, austere, and of disciplined senses—

sanskrit: jñānadagdhaparikleśaḥ prayogaratir ātmavān niṣpracāreṇa manasā paraṃ tad adhigacchati
english: his afflictions burned away by knowledge, delighting in the practice, and self-possessed—he attains, through a mind grown still, to that Supreme.

sanskrit: dhṛtimān ātmavān buddhiṃ nigṛhṇīyād asaṃśayam mano buddhyā nigṛhṇīyād viṣayān manasātmanaḥ
english: Steadfast and self-possessed, without doubt let him restrain the intellect; let him restrain the mind by the intellect, and the objects of his senses by the mind.

sanskrit: nigṛhītendriyasyāsya kurvāṇasya mano vaśe devatās tāḥ prakāśante hṛṣṭā yānti tam īśvaram
english: For him whose senses are restrained and who brings his mind under his sway, those deities shine forth; rejoicing, they approach him as their lord.

sanskrit: tābhiḥ saṃsaktamanaso brahmavat saṃprakāśate etaiś cāpagataiḥ sarvair brahmabhūyāya kalpate
english: To him whose mind is joined with them, it shines forth as Brahman itself; and when all of these have departed, he is fitted to become one with Brahman.

sanskrit: atha vā na pravarteta yogatantrair upakramet yena tantramayaṃ tantraṃ vṛttiḥ syāt tat tad ācaret
english: Or else, should he not so proceed, let him set out by the disciplines of yoga; whatever course of practice would yield him a way of life made up of such discipline, that let him follow.

sanskrit: kaṇapiṇyākakulmāṣaśākayāvakasaktavaḥ tathā mūlaphalaṃ bhaikṣaṃ paryāyeṇopayojayet
english: Broken grain, oil-cake, sour gruel, herbs, barley-meal, and parched grain, and likewise roots, fruit, and alms—let him take these in turn.

sanskrit: āhāraṃ niyataṃ caiva deśe kāle ca sāttvikam tat parīkṣyānuvarteta yat pravṛtty anuvartakam
english: And food that is measured, suited to place and time, and pure (sāttvika)—having tested it, let him keep to that which sustains his right activity.

sanskrit: pravṛttaṃ noparundheta śanair agnim ivendhayet jñānendhitaṃ tato jñānam arkavat saṃprakāśate
english: Let him not check what has begun, but kindle it slowly as one kindles a fire; then knowledge, fed by knowledge, shines forth like the sun.

sanskrit: jñānādhiṣṭhānam ajñānaṃ trīṃl lokān adhitiṣṭhati vijñānānugataṃ jñānam ajñānād apakṛṣyate
english: Ignorance, founded upon knowledge, stands over the three worlds; but knowledge, attended by discernment, is drawn out from ignorance.

sanskrit: pṛthaktvāt saṃprayogāc ca nāsūyur veda śāśvatam sa tayor apavargajño vītarāgo vimucyate
english: Through their separateness and their conjunction the man free of envy knows the eternal; knowing the deliverance from both, freed of passion, he is released.

sanskrit: vayotīto jarāmṛtyū jitvā brahma sanātanam amṛtaṃ tad avāpnoti yat tad akṣaram avyayam
english: Passed beyond his years, having conquered old age and death, he attains the eternal Brahman, that deathless, imperishable, and unchanging.

sanskrit: gurur uvāca niṣkalmaṣaṃ brahmacaryam icchatā carituṃ sadā nidrā sarvātmanā tyājyā svapnadoṣān avekṣatā
english: The teacher said: He who wishes ever to practice stainless chastity, mindful of the faults of dreaming, must utterly forsake sleep with his whole being.

sanskrit: svapne hi rajasā dehī tamasā cābhibhūyate dehāntaram ivāpannaś caraty apagatasmṛtiḥ
english: For in dream the embodied self is overcome by passion and by darkness, and, as though it had entered another body, wanders about with its memory gone.

sanskrit: jñānābhyāsāj jāgarato jijñāsārtham anantaram vijñānābhiniveśāt tu jāgaraty aniśaṃ sadā
english: By the practice of knowledge he keeps awake at once for the sake of inquiry; and through his fixed devotion to discernment he keeps awake without rest, always.

sanskrit: atrāha ko nv ayaṃ bhāvaḥ svapne viṣayavān iva pralīnair indriyair dehī vartate dehavān iva
english: Here one may ask: what is this state, wherein in dream the embodied self, with its senses dissolved, yet moves as though amid sense-objects and as though it had a body?

sanskrit: atrocyate yathā hy etad veda yogeśvaro hariḥ tathaitad upapannārthaṃ varṇayanti maharṣayaḥ
english: To this it is replied: even as Hari, the lord of yoga, knows this, so do the great sages set it forth with reasoned meaning.

sanskrit: indriyāṇāṃ śramāt svapnam āhuḥ sarvagataṃ budhāḥ manasas tu pralīnatvāt tat tad āhur nidarśanam
english: The wise declare that dream, which pervades all, comes from the weariness of the senses; and because the mind is then absorbed, they call this and that within it mere appearance.

sanskrit: kāryavyāsaktamanasaḥ saṃkalpo jāgrato hy api yadvan manorathaiśvaryaṃ svapne tadvan manogatam
english: As for one whose mind clings to its tasks there is intention even while awake, so the sovereignty of his desires that is present in the mind appears likewise in dream.

sanskrit: saṃsārāṇām asaṃkhyānāṃ kāmātmā tad avāpnuyāt manasy antarhitaṃ sarvaṃ veda sottamapūruṣaḥ
english: The man whose self is made of desire would attain that, amid countless rounds of existence; but he who is the supreme person knows all that lies hidden within the mind.

sanskrit: guṇānām api yad yat tat karma jānāty upasthitam tat tac chaṃsanti bhūtāni mano yad bhāvitaṃ yathā
english: Whatever work of the guṇas he knows to be at hand, that very thing living beings foretell, according as the mind has been made disposed.

sanskrit: tatas tam upavartante guṇā rājasatāmasāḥ sāttviko vā yathāyogam ānantaryaphalodayaḥ
english: Then there come upon him the qualities, whether of passion and darkness or of goodness, each as it fits, with its fruit arising in unbroken sequence.

sanskrit: tataḥ paśyaty asaṃbaddhān vātapittakaphottarān rajastamobhavair bhāvais tad apy āhur duranvayam
english: Then he beholds incoherent things, dominated by wind, bile, and phlegm; and that too, arising from states born of passion and darkness, they call hard to follow.

sanskrit: prasannair indriyair yad yat saṃkalpayati mānasam tat tat svapne 'py uparate manodṛṣṭir nirīkṣate
english: Whatever the mind intends through senses grown serene, that very thing, even in dream when activity has ceased, the mind's eye beholds.
